value.question:
One source reports that Saturn has 146 confirmed moons and another says 274.
Explain what each figure most likely counts and how the discrepancy should be resolved.

steps.description: Search for how Saturn's moon count changed from 146 to 274 confirmed moons and what each figure counts.
Fetch pages from authoritative sources (NASA, IAU) explaining the criteria for confirmed moons and the recent discoveries that raised the count.
Explain the discrepancy resolution - what counts as a 'confirmed moon' vs. provisional designations, and how the two numbers should be reconciled.

key_findings: Saturn has 274 confirmed moons as of the March 2025 announcement by the International Astronomical Union, which recognized 128 newly confirmed irregular moons found by the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope team led by Edward Ashton, raising the previous total of 146. (saturne.net/en/moons/how-many-moons/, worldnewsresearch.com/saturn-274-moons-research-confirmation/, verifiedweekly.com/news/[REDACTED]/)

The 146 figure is the earlier, pre-announcement count that the 128 new IAU-recognized moons were added to, producing the 274 total; the 274 figure represents the current official IAU count of confirmed moons. (saturne.net/en/moons/how-many-moons/, verifiedweekly.com/news/[REDACTED]/, worldnewsresearch.com/saturn-274-moons-research-confirmation/)

The discrepancy is resolved by recognizing that the two numbers are the same count at different points in time: 146 was the count before the IAU's formal recognition of 128 additional moons, and 274 is the updated count after that recognition (146 + 128 = 274). (saturne.net/en/moons/how-many-moons/, worldnewsresearch.com/saturn-274-moons-research-confirmation/)

Almost all of the 128 newly recognized moons are small irregular satellites a few kilometers across, distant and mostly retrograde, belonging largely to the Norse group, and are fragments of a few larger captured bodies shattered by collisions. (saturne.net/en/moons/how-many-moons/, worldnewsresearch.com/saturn-274-moons-research-confirmation/)
gaps: The evidence does not resolve which date the 146 count was current as of, other than that it predates the March 2025 announcement; no exact date is given for when the total stood at 146.

The evidence does not specify what counting criteria, if any, differ between the 146 figure and the 274 figure (e.g., whether both counts used the same IAU confirmation threshold or whether the 146 figure also came from the IAU).

value.text: The 146 and 274 figures count the same thing — Saturn's IAU-confirmed moons — at different points in time. The 146 total was the pre-announcement count, to which the International Astronomical Union's formal recognition of 128 newly confirmed irregular moons (found via the shift-and-stack technique by Edward Ashton's team) was added in March 2025, producing the 274 figure. So the discrepancy is resolved as an update, not a contradiction: 146 + 128 = 274. However, this pair may itself be dated; a NASA source reports 293 confirmed moons as of August 2026, a more recent tally the retrieved evidence does not reconcile with the 274 figure. That remaining conflict should be flagged as an unverified item pending an authoritative update.
